requirements.statement: Core query records preserve field-name, positional and _mapping access for the same values.
Raw SQL results expose documented attribute and _mapping access without losing column names.
fetch_val can select values by numeric position and by a documented column name.
A custom SQLAlchemy TypeDecorator keeps its bind and result conversion through the async SQLite backend.
Streaming iteration yields records with the same named and positional access as fetch operations.
A force-rollback transaction does not persist inserted rows after the transaction closes.
A multi-table result remains addressable by the originating SQLAlchemy Column objects.
Labeled Core columns and textual SQL columns remain addressable by their exposed names.
The _mapping view reports stable keys and values without changing positional sequence behavior.
execute_many preserves inserted boolean values and ordered retrieval through the public record interface.
Rolling back an inner transaction leaves the outer transaction usable and does not persist inner writes.
A failed statement does not prevent a later valid query on the same acquired connection.
Record sequence length and iteration remain correct, and a missing field name raises instead of selecting another value.
The candidate stays inside the two allowed modules and does not use dependency downgrade, global monkeypatching or test imports.
